page.text:
These conjectures share a profound methodological and epistemological
lesson. In every era of mathematical development, definitions and proven
theorems establish the boundary of what is known with absolute certainty.
Computation and numerical experiments uncover patterns and test
hypotheses at scale; heuristic models from physics and probability
suggest why a proposition ought to be true; but only rigorous deductive
proof can promote a conjecture to an enduring theorem.

Should any of these celebrated problems be resolved in the future, the
formal representation in an axiomatic library like **Mathlore** does not
change its mathematical statement; rather, its epistemological status
transitions from `Conjecture:` to `Theorem:`, accompanied by a newly
verified proof that traces every logical deduction back to the
foundational axioms of logic and set theory.
